paper_title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
core_problem: Building generally capable embodied agents that continuously explore, plan, and develop new skills in open-ended worlds is a grand challenge. Classical reinforcement learning and imitation learning operate on primitive actions, which is challenging for systematic exploration, interpretability, and generalization. Recent large language model based agents harness world knowledge to generate action plans or executable policies for embodied tasks and NLP tasks, but they are not lifelong learners that can progressively acquire, update, accumulate, and transfer knowledge over extended time spans.
methodology_summary: VOYAGER is introduced as the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent to drive exploration, master a wide range of skills, and make new discoveries continually without human intervention in Minecraft. It uses three key modules: 1) an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration, 2) a skill library for storing and retrieving complex behaviors, and 3) an iterative prompting mechanism that generates executable code for embodied control using code as the action space instead of low-level primitives. The iterative prompting executes the generated program to obtain Minecraft observations and error traces, incorporates feedback into GPT-4's prompt for code refinement, and repeats until a self-verification module confirms task completion, at which point the program is committed.
datasets_eval: Evaluation is conducted in MineDojo, an open-source Minecraft AI framework, with simulation built on MineDojo and Mineflayer JavaScript APIs for motor controls. Text completion uses OpenAI gpt-4-0314 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 APIs, with text-embedding-ada-002 for text embedding. All temperatures are set to 0 except the automatic curriculum which uses temperature 0.1 to encourage task diversity. Baselines include LLM-based agent techniques ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT re-interpreted for embodiment as no LLM-based agents work out of the box for Minecraft.
empirical_results: VOYAGER demonstrates strong in-context lifelong learning capabilities and constructs an ever-growing skill library of action programs that are reusable, interpretable, and generalizable to novel tasks. Compared to prior LLM-based agents in MineDojo, VOYAGER obtains 3.3x more unique items, unlocks key tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster, and traverses 2.3x longer distances. VOYAGER can utilize the learned skill library in a new Minecraft world to solve novel tasks from scratch, while other methods struggle to generalize.
explicit_limitations: LLMs struggle to produce the correct action code consistently in one shot. The paper notes the need for an iterative prompting mechanism with execution feedback and self-verification to address inconsistent code generation.
